input.quote: Except to the extent any jointly-owned inventions or intellectual property are included in subject matter licensed by one Party to the other Party under this Agreement, each Party may only practice any such jointly-owned inventions or intellectual property for its own internal purposes, and neither Party shall have the right to enforce, license, or assign such jointly- owned inventions or intellectual property, without the prior written consent of the other Party.
input.rationale: Ownership is otherwise sound for us: Section 11.1(a) leaves Ono owning IP made solely by Ono personnel, Section 2.6's Grant-Back is only a non-exclusive, Product-limited licence (no assignment of Ono IP or Improvements), Sections 4.7-4.8 exchange Data by licence/right of reference rather than transfer, Ono owns its INDs and Marketing Approvals (4.2(b)-(c)), and Article XII has Array assigning Product Trademarks to Ono. The failure is Section 11.1(c)-(d): jointly-created inventions are jointly owned, and 11.1(d) then confines each Party to internal-purpose practice and bars licensing, enforcement or assignment without the other's consent, save where the joint IP happens to fall within the licences granted (for Ono, only Products in the Ono Territory). That is joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit, which the playbook treats as walk-away territory, so it fails the fallback. The redline keeps the collaboration's joint-ownership architecture (deleting it outright would be disproportionate here) but restores an unrestricted right to practise, exploit and license co-owned IP, subject to the exclusive licences already granted, while retaining a consent gate on assigning a co-ownership interest.

proposal.summary: Give each Party an unrestricted right to exploit and license jointly-owned inventions, removing the internal-use-only limitation and consent requirement.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 11.1(c) creates joint ownership, but 11.1(d) then limits us to internal use of that jointly-owned IP and blocks any licensing without Array's consent. We need an unrestricted right to practise, exploit and license our own co-owned inventions (subject to the exclusive licences already granted), which our playbook treats as the minimum acceptable alternative to no joint ownership at all; we have kept a consent requirement on outright assignment of a co-ownership interest, which protects both Parties.

ops.oldText: Except to the extent any jointly-owned inventions or intellectual property are included in subject matter licensed by one Party to the other Party under this Agreement, each Party may only practice any such jointly-owned inventions or intellectual property for its own internal purposes, and neither Party shall have the right to enforce, license, or assign such jointly- owned inventions or intellectual property, without the prior written consent of the other Party.
ops.newText: Subject only to the exclusive licenses expressly granted under this Agreement, each Party shall have the unrestricted right to practice, use and otherwise exploit, and to grant licenses and sublicenses under, any such jointly-owned inventions and intellectual property for any purpose, without the consent of, and without any obligation to account to, the other Party; provided that neither Party shall assign its interest in such jointly-owned inventions or intellectual property, other than to an Affiliate or in connection with a permitted assignment of this Agreement, without the prior written consent of the other Party.
